readings: Reset is synchronous: registers clear only on the rising clock edge when rst is low.
Reset is asynchronous: registers clear immediately when rst goes low, independent of clk.
ins, ad1, and ad2 are combinational assignments from the internal registers, so they update in the same cycle as the register write.
ins, ad1, and ad2 are registered outputs, adding one clock cycle of latency after the internal registers update.

ambiguities.aspect: Mapping of outputs to internal registers
readings: ins and ad1 are always derived from ins_p1 (first source), and ad2 is always derived from ins_p2 (second source), regardless of fetch.
ins and ad1 are derived from whichever register was most recently written (ins_p1 for fetch=01, ins_p2 for fetch=10), while ad2 is from ins_p2 only.
ad2 is always the registered value of ins_p2, so it updates one cycle after fetch=2'b10 is applied.
ad2 is a combinational pass-through of the data input when fetch=2'b10, updating in the same cycle.
